implementation_notes: The IDL toolchain generates the transport-facing client stub that hides framing, serialization and connection setup; a thin local class owns one channel/stub, sets a deadline on every ClientContext and translates grpc::Status into a domain error while retaining its code and message. The generated stub is not automatically a domain delegate: wrap it when the caller needs a narrower contract, batching, auth context or error policy. Prefer this for new service-to-service work with a protobuf contract; channel reuse and gRPC service configuration replace most classic lookup code.
pitfalls: A ClientContext belongs to exactly one call and must not be shared or reused across threads.
Without a deadline a call can hang forever; set one per call (or rely on a server-side default).
The channel is expensive to create and thread-safe once created - build one per target and share it instead of dialling per request.

variants.name: Hand-written OO delegate over a bespoke transport
variants.idiom_name: abstract service interface + delegate caching a hand-built service handle
variants.implementation_notes: The classic form: a pure-virtual service interface the client depends on, a delegate implementation that resolves the service once through a lookup abstraction, caches the handle, invokes through a transport object and catches transport exceptions to rethrow domain errors. Choose it when no IDL/generated client exists (legacy CORBA/SOAP, in-house RPC) or when the delegate must own retry/circuit-breaker policy; std::function can replace the interface where delegation is a single callback instead of a service. The sketch uses C++17 for std::optional; a C++11 implementation can replace it with an explicit validity flag.
pitfalls: A handle cached across failover points at a dead target; re-resolve on transport error instead of retrying the same handle.
Guard only the handle cache (std::once_flag/std::mutex around lookup), not the whole delegate - a broad lock serializes every client call.
Reference cycles between the delegate and a cached handle leak memory; keep the cached handle weakly owned or owning only.
